title: Chicken Casserole with Cider and Tarragon
subtitle: A creamy autumn braise
excerpt: Chicken thighs braised in dry cider with tarragon and a splash of cream. The sauce is mellow, slightly sweet, and fragrant with aniseed herb. Serve with buttered rice or crusty bread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken braised in cider is a classic of Norman and Western French cooking, brought into the British kitchen through the apple-growing counties. Tarragon appears in many French-influenced British recipes for chicken from the mid-twentieth century.

recipeTools.notes: A heavy pot with a lid for an even braise on the hob or in the oven.

content.text: Chicken and cider casserole is a gentle braise of bone-in chicken thighs in dry cider finished with cream and fresh tarragon. The cider gives the sauce a soft sweetness without any sharpness, and the tarragon adds a clean, faintly aniseed note. It cooks in about an hour on the hob or in a low oven.

Season the chicken thighs all over with salt and pepper. Heat the oil and butter in a large dutch oven over a medium-high heat. Brown the thighs, skin-side down first, for about 5 minutes per side until golden. Lift out and set aside.
Pour away most of the fat, leaving about a tablespoon. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in the cider and stock. Scrape up the browned bits from the base of the pot. Add the tarragon sprigs and the mustard. Return the chicken to the pot, skin-side up.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover with a lid, and cook over a low heat for 40 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and tender.

Lift the chicken out. Remove and discard the tarragon stalks. Pour in the cream, increase the heat, and simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly. Return the chicken to the pot and heat through.
Strip the leaves from the remaining fresh tarragon and scatter over before serving. Taste and adjust the salt.
